title: Annotatio VI §.III (1): Scultetus — Judas ate bread of Lord by mouth, not Lord-bread by faith
pass_a_gloss: This testimony of Augustine is so lucid that even the most distinguished Scultetus of Hamburg rises to it, saying: If Judas was present at the sacred feast, he ate the bread of the Lord WITH THE MOUTH, but not the bread the Lord by faith. Adding meanwhile: For Judas too the bread was communion of Christ’s body (namely external): For equally to Judas as to the remaining Apostles it was said by Christ — not: This which I give with the bread, but: This, or, this bread, is Christ’s body. Discuss. Univers. Reform. §. 258. p. 160.
pass_b_english: Scultetus of Hamburg rises to that Augustine: if Judas was at the feast, he ate the Lord’s bread with the mouth, not the Lord-bread by faith.
Even for Judas the bread was external communion of Christ’s body — Christ said to him as to the rest, “this bread is my body” (Discuss. Univers. Reform. §.258).
source_text: Testimonium hoc Augustini adeò luculentum est, ut etiam Clarissimus Scultetus Hamburgensis eidem assurgat, dicens: Si Judas interfuit S. epulo, manducavit ille panem Domini ORE, non autem panem Dominum per fidem. Addens interim: Ipsi quoque Judæ, panis fuit communio corporis Christi (puta externa): Æque enim Judæ, ac reliquis Apostolis, dictum est à Christo: Non: Hoc, quod cum pane do, sed; Hoc, seu, hic panis, est corpus Christi. Discuss. Univers. Reform. §. 258. pag. 160.
